chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Habbar from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Isma'il ibn Rabaah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"If you pray while you believe you are within the time, and the time has not yet entered, then the time enters while you are in the prayer, then it has sufficed for you."

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And the beginning of the time of the morning prayer is the emergence of dawn, which is the whiteness, and he said: And for each of the obligatory prayers there are two times.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prayer if one is unsure whether the prayer time has entered?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *sahh al-salat* (validity of prayer) for those praying in a state of doubt regarding the entry of prayer time, provided the time enters during the prayer. Shaykh al-Tusi contextualizes this by defining the precise onset of Fajr as the horizontal spread of dawn light, while also noting the scholarly distinction that each obligatory prayer possesses both an early (*awwal*) and a proper (*dakhil*) time, reflecting the flexibility within Shia fiqh for valid performance.
